xccdf-1.2:Profile.xccdf-1.2:title: CUI, tailored for dc2 (cyberinabox)
xccdf-1.2:Profile.xccdf-1.2:description:
Extends xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_cui with one documented deviation.
Deviation: CCE-83956-3 / rule sysctl_user_max_user_namespaces. The base "cui" profile sets user.max_user_namespaces = 0. On dc2 this conflicts with systemd's own unit-level sandboxing (PrivateUsers=true/yes, used by stock RHEL 9 irqbalance.service and upower.service, plus GNOME session helper units), which requires the ability to create at least one user namespace per sandboxed service and fails with ENOSPC when the kernel-wide limit is 0.
The rule's own upstream description states: "When containers are deployed on the machine, the value should be set to large non-zero value" and warns remediation "might impair or prevent functionality of certain applications ... especially for general container usage and for certain desktop applications." dc2's kickstart installs both @container-management and @graphical-server-environment package groups, i.e. exactly the cases the rule itself calls out.
Deviation applied: /etc/sysctl.d/user_max_user_namespaces.conf sets user.max_user_namespaces = 15000 instead of 0 -- bounded well short of unlimited, but sufficient for systemd unit sandboxing and normal container/session use. This rule is deselected below so scans reflect an intentional, documented exception rather than an unexplained fail.
Approved by: Don Shannon. Date: 2026-09-14.
Note: this tailoring targets ssg-rl9-ds.xml (the Rocky Linux 9 native SCAP content), not ssg-rhel9-ds.xml. The original 2026-08-15 kickstart's %addon com_redhat_oscap block referenced ssg-rhel9-ds.xml, whose platform/CPE data is scoped to cpe:/o:redhat:enterprise_linux:9 and does not match this host's actual cpe:/o:rocky:rocky:9::baseos identity -- confirmed empirically: evaluating the base cui profile against ssg-rhel9-ds.xml yields zero pass/fail results (everything reports notapplicable/notselected), while the same profile against ssg-rl9-ds.xml yields real pass/fail results. Future compliance scans on this host should use ssg-rl9-ds.xml.
